judgments.evidence: src/readers.jl:38 reads 'Only cells and stores are addressable (§5.2, §8.3).' The spec's own statement at design/spec.md:13328-13330 cites §4.2 and §8.3 for the same rule. §5.2 (spec.md:1138) covers the homes of the bundle views, 'Each datum has exactly one home', and says nothing on addressability. When readers.jl was added (21d99219), the spec of that commit (docs/framework_spec.md:7774) read 'only cells are addressable (§5.2)'. The spec has since moved the cite to §4.2, 'Consumers see ports, not stages', which fixes the port as the addressable unit (spec.md:920-922). The code comment was never updated.
judgments.fix: Only cells and stores are addressable (§4.2, §8.3).
judgments.note: The Design lines at src/readers.jl:25 and :492 also list §5.2. They head whole blocks, and §5.2 can stand there for the homes of the stores and cells. Only the inline cite at :38 is plainly wrong. Swapping §5.2 for §4.2 in those two lines too would match the spec's cite, but that is a separate call.

judgments.evidence: src/readers.jl:696-698 refuses a StoreSelector (GetState or GetDeriv, :151) under a :table source as ReadResolution :store_selector. Probe CV7b_v/probe.jl lines '004 table get_state' and '004 table get_deriv' give [(:ReadResolution, :store_selector)]. 'series get_state' through the snapshot reader gives the same. '004 exec get_state ok' resolves under an executor.

src/readers.jl:190, 215, 244, 270 and 296 define get_state/get_deriv/get_output(path, leaf = "") and get_input/get_face(leaf = ""). Appendix B at design/spec.md:15343-15344 writes the same five signatures. The probe's 'methods' and 'defaults' lines confirm the one- and two-argument methods with the empty default.

src/readers.jl:801-805 gives the headless head the default face y through _read_shape(::GetOutput). Probe results: a bare SVector port read headless ('013 headless bare-y spin whole') and as "[2]" both resolve. An assembly path gives :assembly_path, an undeclared port :undeclared and a bad step :not_indexable, all ReadResolution. A headless read on named ports ('013 headless on named ports', and acc with y_types (y = Float64,)) gives ReadResolution :port_shape. Under both :table and executor sources the read resolves.

src/readers.jl:530 reads(; selectors...) = _reads(NamedTuple(selectors)) -> Reads. Lines :532-539 refuse a non-selector as ReadSetMisuse :not_a_selector (probe '022 non-selector'). Probe '022 unknown path' and '022 series unknown path' give PathResolution :unknown_child, and '022 other' gives ReadResolution :undeclared. The docstring names the slurped selectors in prose with an example and has no keyword bullet, as docstring_rules.md:56-57 (rule 5) prescribes.

design/rules/docstring_rules.md:56-57 says 'A slurped kw... whose names the caller chooses takes prose and no bullet.' The reads docstring (src/readers.jl:509-528) has the signature 'reads(; selectors...) -> Reads', which mirrors the definition at :530 (rule 7). It has no # Keywords list and describes the labels in prose ('A read set names each selector under a label, as in ...').

design/code_map.md:1079-1085 matches the code. Each entry carries its chain C as a type parameter (src/readers.jl:572-586). CellRead's _read runs over a StoreBundle (:602), which dataplane.jl:587 shares for snapshots. The source keyword exists, and :696 refuses a StoreSelector under :table. @nospecialize(read_set::Reads) appears on _compile_reads (:665), _resolve_reads (:684) and _mount (:739). The 'Reader{T}' wording abbreviates struct Reader{T,L,E} (:621) and is not wrong.

src/readers.jl:789 gives get_state's headless head the letter x on the continuous tier and s on the discrete tier, read from state_decls (src/build.jl:33: decl.x or decl.s). get_deriv (:797) takes x. No path reaches an m store. Probe results: get_state("latch", :m) on BareLatch, which has a bare m_init, gives ReadResolution :undeclared. get_state("src") on a component with only a mode store gives :store_shape, and get_state("src", :phase) gives :undeclared. The spec agrees with the code elsewhere: §14.8 at design/spec.md:13682-13683 says get_state and get_deriv are 'validated against x_init/s_init'. design/pending.md has no bullet that owes a mode-store selector.
judgments.fix: §14.4 (spec.md:13280-13281): 'A bare store (a store declared as one leaf) has the field `x`, `s` or `m`, and a headless store-selector address may stand for a bare `x` or `s`, the stores the selectors read.' Appendix B (spec.md:15347): 'The empty default stands for a bare store's letter, `x` or `s`, or a bare contract's default face, `u` or `y`.'
judgments.backing_entry: D-438 (design/log.md:18252). Its title and Position name the letters x, s or m for a bare store, and its readers bullet speaks of a bare store generally without leaving m out. Its examples and every reader rule cover x and s only.

notes: I edited no tracked files. The probe script is /Users/miguel/.julia/dev/Redstone.jl/design/reports/20261124_doc_conformance/probes/CV7b_v/probe.jl and its output is in out.txt in the same folder. It ran three times: two runs stopped on probe-side errors and the last ran in full. I copied the readable() fixture into it from test/test_readers.jl, because test/fixtures.jl does not define it. Two non-conformances: CV7b-003, drift (the spec moved its addressability cite from §5.2 to §4.2 after readers.jl was written), and CV7b-028, deviation (no selector reads an m store, but §14.4 and Appendix B name m among the letters a headless address stands for).
